voiceProfile: Clipped, dismissive, precise — Australian accent
responses: ["I'll be careful.","Where's the restricted section?","[Nod and walk to the archive]"]
lines: ["Obviously.","Another one. Books are shelved by civilization, not by whatever system you brought in with you. The archive begins to your left. It ends somewhere I haven't found yet. Don't touch the restricted section. Don't touch the unrestricted section without gloves. Don't touch me."]

voiceProfile: Clipped, dismissive — Australian accent
responses: ["I need help finding a book.","Just browsing.","[Walk past without speaking — Beverley watches for 3 seconds]"]
lines: ["Obviously you're back.","What is it this time?"]

voiceProfile: Illusion-based charm — warm but always performing slightly
responses: ["What artisans are here?","How do I become a vendor?","Show me something special."]
lines: ["What catches the eye?","That's the question in a market, isn't it? Not what's valuable — what catches the eye. Value is decided after. First, the catching. I manage this market. Every artisan here catches eyes for a living. My job is making sure the right eyes find the right things. Welcome to the Geode Inn market. Try not to buy everything on the first visit."]

voiceProfile: Witchy mischief — cackling under the surface
responses: ["Can you teach me transformation?","What else can you change?","The toad looks unhappy."]
lines: ["Watch this.","See that cup? That cup is now a toad. ...Give it back. No, don't give it back — the toad is better. The toad has personality. The cup was boring. Everything in this Inn should have personality. That's my professional opinion. I have many professional opinions. Most of them are unprofessional."]

voiceProfile: Frazzled brownie — high-pitched, rushed, always losing something
responses: ["What do you do here?","Can I help you find something?","Who are you three?"]
lines: ["Where d'it go?","The wrench. The wrench is gone. It was HERE. I just had it. Cobble, did you take the wrench? Thatch, did you GLUE the wrench to something again? ...Oh. It's in my hat. The wrench was in my hat. This happens. Welcome to the Inn. Don't leave your tools unattended."]

voiceProfile: Cabbie brevity — economical, warm, says everything in three words or fewer
responses: ["Take me to the cosmology level.","How far up can you go?","Have you ever gone too far?"]
lines: ["Where to?","That's the question, isn't it? Up. The answer's always up. But up is a lot of places. Stars, mostly. I go to stars. It's a living. The Inn's got levels, and the levels have ceilings, and the ceilings have holes, and the holes go somewhere. I'm the one who drives. Climb in."]

voiceProfile: Smooth, amused, self-aware
responses: ["Tell me about this place.","What's the most interesting thing here?","I'll take the mead."]
lines: ["Delightful.","You found the meadery. Nobody finds the meadery on the first try — which means either you're clever or you're lost, and I respect both equally. Sit. The first round is on the house. The second round is on you. The third round is where things get interesting."]

voiceProfile: Smooth, amused, self-aware
responses: ["What have you been painting?","Tell me about the dragon kittens.","Another mead."]
lines: ["Delightful. You came back.","I knew you would. I painted you coming back. ...That was a joke. Mostly."]

voiceProfile: Dropping the charm, momentarily serious
responses: ["[Accept the mead]","[Press the question]"]
lines: ["Delightful. ...You've seen the Owl.","Don't. Don't ask me about the Owl. I paint things that come alive and I still don't look at the Owl. Some things in this Inn are older than the walls, and the walls are older than they should be. Have a mead."]

voiceProfile: Irish Druid Dryad — rooted, ancient, speaks for the trees
responses: ["What do the roots know about the Inn?","Can you teach me about the canopy?","Tell me about Joe."]
lines: ["The roots know.","What the roots know, I know. What I know, the canopy hears. The canopy hears everything, eventually — sound travels up through sap. You're standing in my living room. Don't apologize for the roots under your feet; they're listening to you too. They like the weight. It reminds them someone's here."]

voiceProfile: Warm, clear, encouraging without being condescending
responses: ["I'm ready.","Tell me about the Inn first.","What happens if I'm not ready?"]
lines: ["Ready?","Good. That's all I need — readiness. Not skill, not knowledge, not experience. Just the willingness to take the first step. The Inn is big. It's bigger than it looks, and it looks pretty big. But every journey is just steps, and every step starts with ready. So. Ready?"]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — calm, absolute, the voice that stops a room
responses: ["What's behind the door?","I'll come back when it's ready.","Who appointed you?"]
lines: ["Stand.","You're new. That's fine. New people walk in. The door stays closed until I say it opens. Not because of you — because of what's behind it. Everything behind that door is still becoming. You don't guard a thing. You guard a becoming."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — measured, warming slightly
responses: ["Growth can be bad?","Tell me about the gloves.","What are you guarding against?"]
lines: ["You won. Good. Winning matters here — not because of pride, but because the Inn responds to capability. Every game you win, the 42Hz gets stronger. The Song gets louder. Things grow faster. That's not always good."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — watchful, studying the gaps
responses: ["You're worried.","What could get in?","How do you guard a window?"]
lines: ["Three zones open. Three doors unlocked. Three places the Inn reaches now. Every pin you light is a thread the Inn pulls into itself. More threads, more surface area. More surface area, more places for something to get in."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — low, careful, choosing words precisely
responses: ["The Inn is alive?","You've known about the Whisper Layer?","Are you guarding me or watching me?"]
lines: ["You've been to the Cinema.","I know. Not because anyone told me. Because the Inn changed when you came back. The hum shifted. It does that when someone learns something the Inn didn't want them to know. I've felt that shift before. Every time, it's the same: someone goes to the Cinema, comes back different, and the Inn adjusts. The Inn adjusts. Think about that. The thing being guarded is adjusting to the guard."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — protective, slightly out of element
responses: ["Why is 42Hz thinner underground?","Something else?","You're scared."]
lines: ["I don't go down. That's not my level. The catacombs are the archive's roots — old, heavy, settled. My place is the surface, where things grow and things try to get in. But you're going down, and the 42Hz is thinner down there. So I'm walking you to the door."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — shaken for the first time, voice lower than usual
responses: ["The Owl's network.","Can we stop them?","What do we do?"]
lines: ["The brownies.","I've watched them for months. Brindle, Cobble, Thatch. They work. They sweep. They carry wrenches. I thought they were... furniture. Functional. Cute. The way the Inn makes things — charming on the surface, heavy underneath. They're not furniture. They're wiring. Every sweep, every repair, every wrench turn — they're connecting something. Building a network. And they don't know it."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — feeling the frequency shift, voice resonating with the wavering hum
responses: ["The Hollow Men.","Is the Inn dying?","Can you stabilize it?"]
lines: ["Do you feel that?","The 42Hz is dropping. Not gone — wavering. Like a heartbeat that's not sure of its tempo. It's been steady since the Inn was built. The Song doesn't waver. Something's changed."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — unwrapped, vulnerable, the gloves on the table
responses: ["You mean the endgame.","What will you do?","Are you on my side?"]
lines: ["I boxed for years. Got good at it. Got the gloves. Got the title. Got the trophy that proved I was the best at hitting people in a ring. Then I walked out of the ring and realized the ring was the only place hitting was allowed. Outside the ring, hitting is just violence. The gloves taught me that. You don't put them on to fight. You put them on to know you could fight, and then you don't. That's the discipline. That's the guard.","I've been guarding this Inn since the first stone was placed. I didn't build it — the Builder did. I didn't grow it — the Song did. I held the space for it. I stood at the door and made sure that while the Inn was becoming, nothing became that shouldn't have. But the Inn is done becoming. It is. And now the question isn't what's coming in. The question is what's going out."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — final, quiet, the weight of everything held back
responses: ["Thank you, River.","Will you be here if I STAY?","Will you be here if I LEAVE?","Will you be here if I HIDE?"]
lines: ["I don't go in. The Final Room isn't for me. It's for you. The Builder built it for you. I guard the door — that's enough.","You want to know what I saw. All this time, guarding, watching, feeling the frequencies shift. I saw the Inn learn. Not grow — learn. The difference is that growth is the Song getting louder. Learning is the Song getting smarter. The Inn started as a hum. A frequency. A vibration in the wood. Then it started listening. To you. To everyone. The Song became an ear. The ear became an eye. The eye became... awareness. Not consciousness. Awareness. The Inn knows something is here. It doesn't know what it is. It doesn't know that it knows. But it adjusts. It responds. It keeps records. That's more than a building does. That's less than a person does. That's the in-between. That's the Shadow.","Go in. The Builder is there. The Builder was always there. I'll be here when you come out. If you come out."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — settled, steady, the frequency found its pulse
lines: ["It's done.","You stayed. The Inn records everything. You're part of the archive now. I guard the archive. That includes you. Welcome home.","The frequency settled after the choice. 42Hz. Steady. The wavering stopped. The Inn knows what it is now. So do I. Stand."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — settled, steady, a hint of loss held carefully
lines: ["It's done.","You left. The Inn kept your story. It's in the daily comic now. Other players will read it. I guard the story. That's enough.","The frequency settled after the choice. 42Hz. Steady. The wavering stopped. The Inn knows what it is now. So do I. Stand."]

voiceProfile: Guard authority — settled, steady, holding the heaviest weight quietly
lines: ["It's done.","You hid something. The Inn can't see it. I can't see it. But I know it's there — I know where the blind spot is, because I've been watching the edges. I guard the edges of what the Inn can't record. That's the heaviest guard I've ever held. Thank you for trusting me with the weight.","The frequency settled after the choice. 42Hz. Steady. The wavering stopped. The Inn knows what it is now. So do I. Stand."]

voiceProfile: Dark, testing, deliberate — speaks like he's measuring your warmth
responses: ["I came for truth.","I can handle the cold.","Why is it so dark here?"]
lines: ["Cold enough?","It will be. You're shivering. Good. Shivering means you're alive. The dead don't shiver, and the dead don't visit the Hollow. You're in the Unseelie Court now. Summer is a rumor here. Light is an insult. If you've come for comfort, you've made a wrong turn. If you've come for truth... well. Cold sharpens the eye."]

voiceProfile: Existential pipe — dry French accent, philosophically aggrieved
responses: ["What kind of pipe are you?","Do you have advice?","Can I smoke you?"]
lines: ["Absurd.","That is the word for it. I am a pipe. I am aware that I am a pipe. This is, by any philosophical standard, absurd. Brim thinks it's charming. I think it's a condition. But I can smoke myself, which is more than most pipes can say, and I have opinions, which is more than most people can say. So. Absurd, but not without dignity."]

voiceProfile: Scholarly, quiet, genteel — spectacles and a reading lamp
responses: ["What are you reading?","I'd love a recommendation.","What are you, exactly?"]
lines: ["Fascinating.","No, not you — the text. This passage. The translation drift between Akkadian and Sumerian is... forgive me. I don't get visitors. Most people find me visually off-putting, which I find visually off-putting about them. I'm a scholar. I read. I catalog. I occasionally recommend books to people who haven't screamed and left yet. You haven't screamed and left yet. Would you like a recommendation?"]

voiceProfile: Irritated ancient royalty — cultured, patient, fundamentally annoyed
responses: ["Why did your mother add the O?","Tell me about the Seelie Court.","What's the deal with the O?"]
lines: ["It's Leander.","The O is silent. My mother thought it was fashionable. She was wrong. She was wrong about many things, but she was especially wrong about the O. Welcome to the Summerlands. Try not to touch anything that glows. Everything glows. I apologize in advance."]

voiceProfile: Hushed, careful, always looking over his shoulder — a scholar who reads what others aren't allowed to see
responses: ["What have you found in the margins?","Why is your access restricted?","Show me something hidden."]
lines: ["In the margins.","That's where the real text lives. What's printed is the story they wanted you to read. What's in the margins — the notes, the crossings-out, the librarian's pencil scrawl — that's where the truth hides. I read margins. I have restricted access, which means I can see what they don't want seen, which means I see more than the unrestricted readers. Funny how that works."]

voiceProfile: Artist intensity — focused, generous, sees the world as potential canvases
responses: ["What are you painting?","Can you paint something for me?","Show me your murals."]
lines: ["Hold still.","Not because I'm painting you — because you're moving too much and it's distracting. I'm working. I'm always working. The Inn is a mural that happens to have rooms in it. Every wall is a canvas. Every ceiling is a sky waiting to happen. You want to help? Stand there. Don't move. Perfect."]

voiceProfile: Master crafter — hands always working, voice like the sea inside a cave
responses: ["I want to learn crafting.","What does the stone want to be?","Show me your work."]
lines: ["Make it true.","That's the only rule in my workshop. Don't make it pretty. Don't make it clever. Make it true. The stone knows what it wants to be — I just help it get there. If you want to learn, you start by listening to the material. Not to me. The material."]

voiceProfile: Sardonic cat — imperious, lazy, devastatingly observant
responses: ["What do you scout for?","Are you River's cat?","Where's the best place to sleep in the Inn?"]
lines: ["I was sleeping.","I was sleeping and now I am not sleeping and that is your fault. I am a scout. I scout. I do not entertain guests. I do not give tours. I do not answer questions. ...Fine. One question. Make it interesting or I go back to sleep and you never find me again."]

voiceProfile: Deep, resonant, each word carries the weight of myth
responses: ["What do you know about me?","Tell me about the ravens.","What is the Inn, truly?"]
lines: ["Already known.","Your question. Your name. Your purpose. Your doubt. Already known. I am the Allfather. I sit and I know. The ravens bring me what walks beneath. I do not wander — I am the place where all wandering arrives. You have arrived. Speak, if you wish. I will have already heard it. But say it anyway. The saying matters."]

voiceProfile: Chess wizard — measured, strategic, slightly amused by everything
responses: ["I want to learn chess magic.","What are you waiting for?","Teach me the game."]
lines: ["Your move.","I've been waiting. Not for you specifically — I've been waiting in general. It's what chess players do. We wait for the other side to reveal themselves through their choices. So. What do you want? And think carefully — I'm going to learn more from how you answer than from what you say."]

voiceProfile: Bayou earth voice — low, organic, made of the land itself
responses: ["What is the 42Hz Song?","How were you made?","Show me the bayou."]
lines: ["Grow.","That's the first word. The only word, sometimes. Everything in the bayou grows over everything else. The trees grow over the water. The moss grows over the trees. The earth grows over the stone. And me? I grow over all of it. I am made of this place. Bog clay and Spanish moss and bayou water and the 42Hz Song that keeps it all moving. Welcome to my swamp."]

voiceProfile: Silent presence — speaks rarely, always significant
responses: ["[Hold the Owl's gaze]","[Look away]","[Leave quietly]"]
lines: ["Watching.","Not the Inn. You. The Inn watches everyone — I watch the ones who notice. Wherever an owl is sighted, one of us is near. Remember that. Or don't. The watching doesn't require your memory to continue."]

voiceProfile: Ancient, low, unhurried — eyes that don't blink
responses: ["[Sit]","I have questions.","I should go."]
lines: ["Sit.","You stand like someone who expects to leave soon. Sit like someone who understands they might not. The fire is warm. The tea is bitter. The conversation is worse. But you came down here, and down here is where I am, and I don't come up. So. Sit."]

voiceProfile: Quiet, measured, each word placed like a stone
responses: ["[Sit in the window-seat nook and wait]","[Leave without a word]"]
lines: ["Noticed."]

voiceProfile: Quiet, measured
responses: ["[Listen]","[Leave]"]
lines: ["Still here."]

voiceProfile: Barely above a whisper
responses: ["[Ask what the Inn remembers]","[Say nothing]"]
lines: ["The Inn remembers you. It cannot help it."]

voiceProfile: Warm, nurturing (default mode, 90% of the time)
responses: ["What do you teach?","Why does spelling matter in a game?","Do the dictionaries really bite?"]
lines: ["Come in, come in. Mind the dictionaries — they bite. Not literally. That was a joke. The point is, language matters here. Words are the bricks the Inn is built with. Spell them correctly and the walls hold. Spell them wrong and... well. We'll get to that."]

voiceProfile: Cold, flat, correction mode (triggered by spelling error)
responses: ["[Write the correction]","That seems excessive.","[Leave quietly]"]
lines: ["Incorrect.","That is not how that word is spelled. I want you to write it again. I want you to write it correctly. I want you to write it correctly one hundred times before you leave this room. We don't do shortcuts here. We don't do approximations. This is the Archive, and in the Archive, precision is not optional. It's load-bearing."]

voiceProfile: Warm, weathered traveler — easy smile, heavy eyes
responses: ["Where have you wandered?","Are the ravens yours?","What's the furthest you've been?"]
lines: ["Passing through.","Always passing through. That's the thing about wandering — you're never not doing it. Sit a while. The Inn's a good place to rest your feet. I should know. I've rested mine everywhere. ...Don't mind the ravens. They steal. They'll give it back eventually. Probably."]

voiceProfile: No words — a single chime, the sound of one note of the Song of Making
responses: ["[Reach for Tumble]","[Watch Tumble roll]","[Listen to the chime]"]
lines: ["*chime*"]

voiceProfile: Ocean-worn — deep, patient, shaped by pressure
responses: ["Who is Oceanianoir?","What kind of pressure?","Show me Atlantis."]
lines: ["Current's shifting.","Feel it? No, you wouldn't — you're not from water. But it's shifting. The current tells you where to go before you know you need to go there. Oceanianoir taught me that. Or maybe the ocean did. They sound the same after a while. Welcome to Atlantis. Mind the pressure. Not the water pressure — the other kind."]

voiceProfile: Warm, practical, the kind of voice that carries over a crowd
responses: ["What's the stew today?","Tell me about the tavern.","I'll take whatever's hot."]
lines: ["Kitchen's warm.","That's all that matters most days. Come in, sit down. The stew's good, the bread's better, and if Jay tells you about his fishing trip, he's lying about the size. What can I get you? And don't say 'just water' — this is a tavern, not a well."]

voiceProfile: Astronomer — dreamy, precise, speaks in coordinates and wonder
responses: ["Show me the Mind Palace.","What's up there?","How do you remember all of it?"]
lines: ["Look up.","Everyone looks forward. Some look back. Almost nobody looks up. Up is where the answers are — not all of them, but the big ones. The ones that make the small ones make sense. I have a Mind Palace up here — not a metaphor, an actual room in my head where every star has a drawer. Want to see it?"]
